subject: Secure SDLC: ownership map + CI/CD secrets evidence
messages:
From: Marta Leon <marta.leon@finbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinBank Audit Team <audit-team@horizonsec.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SDLC evidence (branch protection, CI agents, secrets controls)

Hi Jordan,

We're running the next tranche of our SIG/SOC2 review and need a focused evidence bundle covering your secure SDLC controls for code review, CI/CD, secrets management, and change approvals. To keep this scoped I have a short checklist — please respond with artifacts or a plan and timeline for delivery by EOD Wed (2028-07-19):

- Branch protection policy and a sample of branch-protection audit logs (last 90 days)
- CI agent inventory and health snapshot (agents, images, regions)
- Secrets scanning results and brief on accept/deny policy for large binaries/credentials in PRs
- Change approval trail for production releases (who approves, where recorded)
- Mapping of commit authors to service owners (commit ownership matrix)
- Any compensating controls for emergency hotfixes (runbooks, postmortems)

A couple of notes: we may ask for redacted excerpts from PRs if there are flagged secrets — it's fine to redact actual token strings. If possible include shared Drive links or CSV/XLS extracts; DocuSign is acceptable for approvals.

Thanks — if you need to loop in engineering contacts please do so. I can also carve out 30 minutes next week to walk through artifacts.

Best,
Marta León
Senior InfoSec Assessor
FinBank Audit Team

Thanks for the checklist. We're on it. Quick plan: I'll deliver a primary bundle by EOD Tues (2028-07-18) and a supplemental file with commit ownership and PR excerpts by Wed morning. Subject: Re: Request: SDLC evidence (branch protection, CI agents, secrets controls)

Jordan/Marta —

Attached: commit-ownership-mapping.xlsx (mapping of repo -> path -> primary owner email; excerpted to top-level services only) and ci_agent_health_snapshot.txt (agent list and last-checkin timestamps). A few clarifications that will help the assessment team:

- Branch protection: we enforce required reviews + linear history for protected branches. The sample audit lines are sanitized; we maintain 90 days of audit logs in CloudAudit and export as CSV on request.

- Secrets scanning: we use a multi-layer approach — pre-commit client-side scanning, server-side scanner on PRs (block on high-confidence matches), and periodic repository scans for legacy commits. High-confidence matches auto-block PR merge until a ticket is opened and remediation is verified. Low-confidence matches are flagged and triaged.

- Rotation/KMS: production model keys are stored in customer-managed HSM/KMS where applicable. For other secrets we use ephemeral short-lived tokens minted by our vault service; rotation cadence is weekly for service tokens, and monthly for application credentials.

- Emergency hotfixes: we maintain a hotfix runbook (internal) and require a post-deployment review within 48 hours; approvals are tracked in JIRA with a standardized label (hotfix:postmortem).

I redacted email addresses in the commit-owner sheet to initials for public delivery; if you need full emails we can provide them in a secure Drive link with viewer restrictions. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cSDLC-evidence

Let me know if you want an auditor service account with read-only access to the artifacts.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Request: SDLC evidence (branch protection, CI agents, secrets controls)

Jordan/Irene —

Received, and thanks for the clear plan and artifacts. The control matrix and commit mapping look useful. A couple of follow-ups before we close this tranche:

- Please include two redacted PR excerpts that were blocked by the server-side scanner in the last 60 days (redact actual token values, show context lines and scanner rule id).
- If possible, provide one example JIRA ticket that documents an emergency hotfix postmortem (redact PII).
- We would prefer auditor read-only access to the Drive folder rather than sending full email lists in-line. Can you create a service account or a shared folder with viewer-only links and notify audit-team@horizonsec.com?

Once we have those three items we'll mark the SDLC evidence request as satisfied and proceed to the next checklist. If it helps, we can take the 30m walkthrough on Wed 7/19 at 10:00 AM PT.

Best,
Marta León
Senior InfoSec Assessor
FinBank Audit Team
